Modified assessment using the Financial Stability Report lens: The FOMC statement rightly notes strong labor markets, solid household spending, and inflation near 2%, and it proceeds with a gradual hike, IOER calibration, and ongoing balance-sheet runoff. However, the Fed’s Financial Stability Report around this period highlights elevated asset valuation pressures, high and rising nonfinancial business leverage with looser underwriting (notably in leveraged loans/CLOs), and bouts of market volatility—while short-term funding risks remain low and banks are well capitalized. These vulnerabilities mean tighter financial conditions from policy normalization could weigh more on future activity than the statement alone conveys, tempering the otherwise positive macro tone. Net tone: cautiously positive, leaning toward neutral.
